\begin{letter}{Admissions Committee\\Department of Mathematics\\Example University\\Pittsburgh, PA 15213}

\opening{Dear Members of the Committee,}

I am writing to apply for the graduate programme in Mathematics beginning
in the autumn of 2027. I will complete my B.S. in Computer Science, with a
minor in Mathematics, in May 2027.

My interest in the programme comes from two directions. As an undergraduate
I worked on line-breaking algorithms and their optimality proofs, which led
me to dynamic programming and, through it, to combinatorial optimisation.
At the same time, a course on real analysis convinced me that I want to
spend the next several years proving things rather than only implementing
them.

During the past year I have been a teaching assistant for an introductory
course on imperative programming. Writing practice exams for forty students
taught me how much a clear proof depends on the order in which the ideas
are presented --- a lesson I expect to apply in a research setting.

I have enclosed my curriculum vitae, transcript and a writing sample.
Letters of recommendation from Professors A.~Author and B.~Coauthor will be
submitted separately. Please do not hesitate to contact me if any part of
the application is missing.

Thank you for your consideration.

\closing{Sincerely,}

\encl{Curriculum vitae; transcript; writing sample}
\cc{Professor A.~Author}
\ps{P.S. My application number is 2027-0412.}
